input:
The performance of the natural-draft tower at the chemical site was logged over the course of one summer month. The approach is defined as the difference between the temperature of the cooled water leaving the tower and the wet-bulb temperature of the air entering it, while the range is the fall in the temperature of the water across the tower, from the hot water entering to the cooled water leaving. Over the month that was logged, the mean wet-bulb temperature was 27 °C, the approach was 6 K and the range was 11 K.

A natural-draft tower relies on buoyancy alone to move its air, and the wet-bulb temperature of the ambient air effectively sets the limit towards which the water can be cooled. The approach therefore indicates how close the tower managed to bring the water to that limit over the month in question, while the range indicates the amount of cooling that the water actually received over the same period. Both figures are monthly means over the logged operation, which means that they describe the tower as it actually ran, at the loads and water rates of that particular month, rather than a rating at some fixed duty. It should also be noted that the cooled water left the tower at the stated approach above the mean wet-bulb temperature throughout the period covered by the logging.

Performance outside the logged month was not measured. In particular, performance at winter wet-bulb temperatures was not measured at all, and the values obtained from the summer logging should not be taken to state what approach or range the tower will hold during the winter.
target:
Performance of the natural-draft tower at the chemical site was logged over one summer month. The approach is the difference between the cooled-water temperature leaving the tower and the wet-bulb temperature of the air entering it. The range is the fall in water temperature across the tower, from the hot water entering to the cooled water leaving. Over the logged month, the mean wet-bulb temperature was 27 °C, the approach was 6 K and the range was 11 K.

A natural-draft tower moves its air on buoyancy alone, and the wet-bulb temperature of the ambient air sets the limit towards which the water can be cooled. The approach states how close the tower brought the water to that limit over the month, and the range states the cooling the water received in the same period. The cooled water left the tower at the stated approach above the mean wet-bulb temperature. Both values are monthly means over the logged operation: the values describe the tower as it ran, at the loads and water rates of that month, and not a rating at a fixed duty.

The two means are read together: a tower that cools through the stated range while holding the stated approach at the logged wet-bulb temperature performed as logged across the whole month, through its hotter and cooler days alike. The logging covers the tower's own operation only; the duty the tower serves sits outside the record. Performance outside the logged month was not measured. In particular, performance at winter wet-bulb temperatures was not measured, and the logged values do not state what approach or range the tower holds in winter.
